audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Singed levels 3, 4-5, first item and two items, and called level 2 even — contradicting five of its own seven whys. whys[1] says she 'controls the level-2 trade window decisively'; whys[2] says her loop is one 'your Mega Adhesive cannot stop'; whys[3] says 'Neither kit is dominant'; whys[5] says her Eclipse spike 'lets her one-rotation you before Rylai's is complete'; whys[6] says the lane becomes 'genuinely even'.
audit.why: At 51.2% over 1080 games this is the closest matchup in the set, and Riven's edge sits in the mid-levels where her three Broken Wings casts, Valor shield and Ki Burst all beat a Singed with no dash. The packet chart reads Skill / Riven / Riven / Skill / Riven / Riven / Skill, which is what the prose actually describes.
audit.corrected: Chart flipped as one group to Skill, Riven, Riven, Skill, Riven, Riven, Skill, with the matching phases sides.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the level-6 comparison was asserted without the numbers that decide it.
audit.why: Blade of the Exile is 120/90/60s while Insanity Potion is a flat 100s. At rank 1 your ultimate comes back twenty seconds before hers — that is the concrete reason the second level-6 fight is yours and the first is not. Broken Wings is 13s flat for the whole three-cast cycle, Ki Burst 11s at rank 1, Valor 10s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: The 120s-vs-100s ultimate gap written into mid, spikes[1] and breakdown.cooldowns, with the basic cooldowns alongside.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings state that Mega Adhesive does not stop her — 'she dashes through the zone before the root procs', 'Mega Adhesive cannot stop', 'Dash through Mega Adhesive with Q-E before the root triggers'. This is backwards on the decisive interaction.
audit.why: Mega Adhesive grounds, and Riot flags both Broken Wings and Valor as dashes, 'mobility that grounding and walls can deny'. She can enter the zone from outside it, but once she is standing in the glue neither her remaining Broken Wings casts nor Valor will fire. The correct instruction is to place the glue under her after she lands, not in front of her as a wall she 'dashes through'. The page taught players their W was useless in the one matchup where it is the whole answer.
audit.corrected: whys[2], spikes[0], wants.foe[0], early and mid rewritten around glue-after-landing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Broken Wings' third cast knocking back was never mentioned, in a matchup where both sides carry displacement.
audit.why: Riot: Broken Wings 'can be reactivated three times in a short time frame with the third hit knocking back nearby enemies'. That third cast will throw you out of your own poison cloud and off the glue you just placed, so the sequencing is: let the third cast go, then glue and Fling. Whoever lands displacement first owns the trade.
audit.corrected: Written into whys[2], dosFull[2] and dontsFull[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Two strings call Wind Slash an 'execute'.
audit.why: Riot's text is 'a powerful ranged attack' — the kit carries no execute flag, only projectile. Calling it an execute teaches a health threshold the file does not support.
audit.corrected: Reworded to name Wind Slash without asserting execute behaviour.

edits.before: Level 6 does not save you in the duel — Riven's Blade of the Exile wind-slash executes you through the Insanity Potion healing if she is ahead or even. Shift entirely into the proxy game: establish a wave behind her tower, farm her minions under the enemy base, and force her to walk away from lane to address you. Every time she chases, she is running into your Poison Trail and a Mega Adhesive that roots her before she reaches melee range — that is the only window you win a direct confrontation. Ghost is mandatory here; without it she simply dashes into your face before you build distance.
edits.after: Level 6 does not save the first duel — Blade of the Exile plus her combo outruns Insanity Potion. But hers is 120s at rank 1 and yours is a flat 100s, so the second level-6 fight is the one you take. Shift into the proxy game meanwhile: establish a wave behind her tower, farm her minions under the enemy base, and force her to walk away from lane to address you. When she chases and lands on you, drop Mega Adhesive on her feet — grounding shuts off her remaining Broken Wings casts and Valor, so she is stuck in the poison with no exit. Ghost is mandatory here; without it she dashes into your face before you build distance.

edits.before: Rylai's Crystal Scepter flips the chase dynamic — now every minion she walks through while hunting your proxy is slowed, and a Fling into the sticky pool roots her long enough for the poison to deal real damage. At two items you are a credible split-push threat she cannot ignore: push a wave, back off, and let the threat of a turret plate force her to rotate instead of fighting on her terms. In a straight 1v1 she can still win if she enters from an angle that avoids your goo zone, so never duel without Mega Adhesive already placed between her and her escape route.
edits.after: Rylai's Crystal Scepter flips the chase dynamic — now every minion she walks through while hunting your proxy is slowed, and a Fling into the sticky pool roots her long enough for the poison to deal real damage. At two items you are a credible split-push threat she cannot ignore: push a wave, back off, and let the threat of a turret plate force her to rotate instead of fighting on her terms. In a straight 1v1 she still wins if she fights outside the goo, so never duel until the glue is already under her and her dashes are grounded.

edits.before: Riven owns this lane physically — she can Q-dash over your Mega Adhesive before the root procs, cancel your Fling setup with W stun, and burst you in the time it takes your poison to tick. Do not stand still and trade with her at levels 1 through 3. Instead, drop Poison Trail through the minion wave for chip damage, and the moment she burns even one Q dash to close, respect the pressure and walk back — she has two more dashes ready. Your job at level 1 is to last-hit cleanly and survive; at level 2 the Fling-glue combo exists, but only throw it when she has already spent her E shield on a trade, never into a fresh kit.
edits.after: Riven owns this lane physically — she enters from outside your glue, cancels your Fling setup with an 11s Ki Burst, and bursts you in the time your poison takes to tick. Do not stand still and trade at levels 1 through 3. Drop Poison Trail through the minion wave for chip damage, and the moment she burns one Broken Wings cast to close, walk back — she has two more, and the third knocks you back. Your job at level 1 is to last-hit cleanly and survive; at level 2 the Fling-glue combo exists, but throw the glue under her feet once she has landed, never in front of her as a wall.

notes: packet suspectName 'Insanity Potion' for riven is a false positive. Level-chart flip proposed as one atomic group of six rows. The reversal on Mega Adhesive is the biggest change here: four strings told the player the glue does not stop Riven, when grounding is in fact the answer — the nuance is that it grounds only while she is standing in it, so it must be placed under her after she lands rather than ahead of her.
